_comment: WC2026 Round of 32, 2026-07-03, Toronto. KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Winner meets the Spain (who beat Austria 3-0) in the Round of 16. Routes: Portugal finished 2nd in Group K (1-1 DR Congo, 4-0 Uzbekistan, 0-0 Colombia; 5 pts, GF 5 GA 1, rating 90) -- a quality side with a SOLID defence (GA 1), but one that can be BLUNT vs an organized block (drew 0-0 Colombia and 1-1 DR Congo) while ROUTING the weak (4-0 Uzbekistan). Croatia finished 2nd in Group L (2-4 England, 1-0 Panama, 2-1 Ghana; 6 pts, GF 5 GA 5, GD 0, rating 84) -- experienced, tactically savvy, tournament-tough (grind-it-out wins over Panama and Ghana), though they shipped 4 in the open loss to England. KEY texture: this is NOT the Austria/rout archetype. Croatia is NOT an open, leaky side that gives the favourite space -- they are an ORGANIZED, control side with genuine knockout pedigree (a habitual extra-time/penalties team), exactly the kind of block that has frustrated Portugal (0-0 Colombia, 1-1 Congo). Class gap ~6 (90 vs 84) -> Portugal a MODERATE favourite, but a close, lower-scoring, DEEP tie with elevated extra-time/penalty risk, not a rout. Portugal the favourite by class + defence; Croatia a dangerous, savvy underdog who thrives when the tie goes long. Home = Portugal (nominal; neutral venue). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

_postmatch.verdict: Clean process hit on side, shape and margin. Portugal advanced as the 60.6% pick, won by the odd goal (2-1 a top-3 scoreline at 9.2%), and Croatia scored exactly as flagged (BTTS Yes 52.6%; 'can score but not prolific'). The TEXTURE read was right: I explicitly said this was NOT the Austria/rout archetype but a close, tighter tie against an organized, savvy Croatia -- a one-goal game (mode 1-1) that Portugal, the moderate favourite, was more likely to nick. It did not need the extra-time/penalty branch I flagged as elevated (27% ET, 14% pens) -- Portugal closed it in regulation -- but that branch being live is exactly why a 2-1 (not a rout) was the expected shape. Contrast with the SAME-DAY Spain 3-0: I correctly separated the rout tie (Spain vs open/leaky Austria) from the grind tie (Portugal vs organized Croatia), and both landed -- a blowout and a one-goal edge respectively.
_postmatch.lesson: Classifying the underdog's SHAPE (organized control side vs open/leaky) is what distinguished this 2-1 grind from the same-day Spain 3-0 rout. Croatia's knockout pedigree and Portugal's bluntness vs blocks correctly produced a tight, one-goal, deep-ish tie rather than a comfortable win -- the favourite advanced, but by the minimum, as the 60.6% (not 80%+) advancement number implied. Don't let a big rating on the favourite pull the forecast toward a rout when the opponent is built to slow the game.
